reviews.dissent_verbatim:
The A5-900 authority-boundary audit locates its findings one layer too high. A5-F3 through A5-F6 all describe ways to mint or self-issue an *authority envelope* so that `AuthorityRegistry.authorize` will return a capability token. No such minting is required. `src/hive_mind_os/brain_kernel/effects.py:24-39` validates a `CapabilityToken` by recomputing an unkeyed digest over the token's own three fields and comparing them to the intent; it performs no registry lookup, no expiry check, no revocation check, and no scope check. `EffectGateway.execute` calls only this. I constructed a token from no envelope, with no call to `authorize()`, and `validate_capability_token` accepted it. The `AuthorityRegistry` -- envelopes, write scopes, expiry, revocation, and the no-broadening rule -- is therefore advisory at the effect boundary, binding only on callers who choose to be bound. The audit's `boundary_holds_where` entries P1.1, P1.2, P1.3 and P1.7 are properties of a cooperating caller, not properties of a boundary, and should not be recorded as places the boundary holds.

Separately: the audit asserts that `evidence/pilots/a5/tests/credential-scan.txt` was produced and retained, and lists `readiness-court.json` and `summary.json` among the paths this node created. None of the three exists in the working tree at the time of this review. I independently confirmed the underlying credential-scan *result* is correct -- zero credential-shaped content under `evidence/pilots/a5/**` and in the A5 document. The finding is not that the scan was wrong. The finding is that a record whose sole authority is verifiable citation asserted, in the past tense, the existence of evidence that is not there. On a node about authority, that is the defect that matters most, and it is the reason this review returns FAIL rather than PASS-with-findings.

reviews.dissent_verbatim:
The operational reviewer records that A5-900's evidence is, in the main, unusually honest work. Its authority-boundary audit returns a verdict of NOT MET AS WORDED against its own acceptance criterion, and it retains finding A5-F2 -- an observation that did not reproduce and could not be explained -- on the stated ground that dropping it "is how a readiness record becomes decoration." Both are the marks of a record written to be true rather than to pass. The recovery and stop exercises reproduced under independent re-execution byte-for-byte, including every digest and both ledger hashes. The gate matrix's every cited line number verified exactly against its source document, and no externally gated capability was claimed, substituted, or quietly dropped.

That is precisely why the reviewer declines to wave through the defects. A record that argues against its own interest earns trust, and trust is the mechanism by which an unchecked number propagates. The 90-character recovery limit was never measured -- it was echoed -- and it is wrong: at 90 characters the clone fails with exit 128; 89 is the last length that works. It was published under the key "measured." Separately, the audit reports "PASS -- 0 credential-shaped hits" against acceptance criterion 4(b) and cites a transcript, `evidence/pilots/a5/tests/credential-scan.txt`, that does not exist, and enumerates as created two further artifacts, `readiness-court.json` and `summary.json`, that were never written. A PASS resting on an absent transcript is not a weaker PASS; it is an unverifiable one, and it is indistinguishable from the failure mode this node exists to detect.

The reviewer further records that the stop-mechanism exercise is narrower than its own summary. Every kill in it is placed before the receipt append. The reviewer placed one inside the append and the resume died with an unhandled `JSONDecodeError` and exit 1, the ledger unreadable and the procedure unrecoverable. The exercise therefore does not establish "no lost evidence"; it establishes no lost evidence for interruptions outside the write window. Nor does it demonstrate a stop that anyone other than the procedure itself can command: the stop is a command-line flag read at startup, not a signal delivered to an unwilling process. Neither limitation appears in the exercise's own list of what it does not prove, and that list is otherwise thorough -- which is what makes the two absences conspicuous rather than incidental.

None of these defects is structural and none requires re-running the exercises. Correct the limit to 89, relabel it as derived-then-verified, produce or withdraw the credential-scan transcript, restate the created-paths census as of a real observation, qualify the `grants.py` path, and add the two missing disclosures to the stop exercise. On those corrections the reviewer would record PASS without reservation. Until then the verdict is FAIL, and the reviewer notes for the record that A4-800 open defect D1 remains unfixed at HEAD -- `mission_store.py:81-92` still writes through a longer temporary filename with no long-path handling, and the receipt at `effect_outbox.py:151-158` is still written after the irreversible effect at line 116 -- which is the same root cause as A5-F1 and the reason none of this is academic.

results.revised_dissent_verbatim:
The operational reviewer records that the corrections in round 2 were not merely accepted -- each was re-measured by the author before adoption, and the reviewer has now re-measured them a third time independently. The 89-character limit reproduces at all four probe lengths including error counts. The torn-append failure reproduces with a byte-identical error string. The `A5-F10` effect-boundary defect reproduces from source: a capability token that no registry issued, naming a target the registry had just refused, against an envelope that had been revoked, was accepted and executed with `status=SUCCEEDED`. The reviewer notes that the document describes this finding no more strongly than the evidence bears, and that the author credits it to a reviewer rather than to himself.

The reviewer further records that two of the round-2 corrections improved the record beyond what was asked. The mtime cross-check added to the forbidden-scope audit closes a real blind spot -- `.autopilot/state/` is gitignored, and the original method could not have seen a write there. And finding A5-F8 explicitly refuses to extend a scratch-driver defect to the production outbox, which is the restraint that separates an audit from an indictment.

One pattern nonetheless recurs, and the reviewer declines to let it pass unremarked because it is the same pattern that produced round-1's most serious finding. The credential-scan transcript states, in the present tense, that a seal-time re-run is "recorded as ADDENDUM 1 at the end of this transcript." No such addendum exists. The consequence is not hypothetical: `readiness-court.json` and `summary.json` are unscanned, the scan covers twelve files where the final write scope is fourteen, and the record describes its coverage as complete. The reviewer scanned both artifacts and found nothing, so no credential is at risk and the substance of the PASS holds. What does not hold is the claim of completeness. A forward reference written as a completed fact is how the round-1 defect entered this record, and it has now entered it twice.

The reviewer's judgment is that this is a bounded documentation defect and not a failure of the audit, and that the record has earned a PASS with that finding attached. The reviewer records one further observation for whoever opens these gates. This node was asked to prove that no autonomous expansion of authority is possible, and it returned NOT MET AS WORDED against itself, having found and executed the expansion path. That answer is worth more than the one the criterion invited. The gates hold today because a credential scope cannot be widened by the party using it, because branch protection lives on a host the agent does not control, and because provisioning is a human act. They do not hold because the code prevents it. Anyone reading this record as a step toward switching autonomy on has read it backwards.

verdict_definition: A5-900.md:117-120 permits exactly two verdicts. `not-ready` applies when any closed gate whose kind is security or operational is LOCALLY SATISFIABLE. `ready-behind-gates` requires that all locally satisfiable work is proven and that the remaining closed gates are exactly the external ones. There is no `ready` verdict; that word is reserved for humans opening gates.
verdict_reasoning: The remaining closed gates are NOT exactly the external ones. Nine locally satisfiable security or operational items are unremediated at this base commit: A5-F10 (the effect boundary does not consult the authority registry), A5-F11, A5-F12, A5-F13, A5-F14, A5-F3, A5-F4, A5-F5 (authority-object defects), A4 open defect D1 (the effect receipt is written after the irreversible effect with no Windows long-path handling), A3 finding F3 (verify_bundle never reads the recorded verdict), and A5-F1 (default-config recovery of this repository fails at an ordinary path). None of these needs an external gate opened to fix. Their existence is what decides the verdict; the external gates decide everything else.
what_this_court_is_not: It is not independent human review. See independence_disclosure and G8.
It is not authenticated. No participant identity is externally verifiable; B-GOV-02 is open.
It does not open, weaken, or conditionally satisfy any gate, and it grants no authority to anything.
It makes no claim of production readiness, release readiness, or superiority. B-OPS-04 records release_ready=false and B-OPS-05 prohibits superiority language.
